issues.failure_explanation: A two-terminal 2-sp graph with vertices x,y,u,v,w and edges a,b parallel between x,y and a 4-edge path x-u-v-w-y is admissible. With terminals x,y, the definition gives w_a=w_b=1 and w_{xu}=w_{uv}=w_{vw}=w_{wy}=phi(4)/phi(1)=8/5. With terminals x,u, the direct edge x-u has weight 1, the two x-y edges have weight phi(5)/phi(2)=5/8, and the remaining path edges have weight phi(5)/phi(1)=1. These weight vectors are not scalar multiples, so the claimed terminal invariance is false.

failure_location.quote: Graph-induced edge weights are invariant to the choice of terminals up to a common factor.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must fix the terminal dependence of G-induced weights (by a corrected definition and proof, or by a fixed terminal convention that still supports the main theorem) and rejustify the star-space construction under that convention.
issues.overall_effect: The G-induced weights are terminal-dependent in a way stronger than a common scale factor, so the matrix W used in the main construction is not well-defined by the stated convention. The proof of the main theorem cannot freely change terminals to the endpoints of an arbitrary tree edge, and the sharpness corollary inherits this failure.
issues.title: G-induced weight invariance under terminal changes is false
issues.why_classification: The invariance claim fails on a small admissible graph, undermining the central weight construction; no source-supported correction preserving the advertised terminal-independence and main theorem is available.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: we will assume the following layout
which completes the proof of the theorem.

issues.failure_explanation: Take the 4-cycle with vertices x,u,v,y and edges a=x-u, b=x-y, c=u-v, d=v-y. Let tau={a,b,c} and e0=b, so the proof chooses terminals x,y. The alternative x-y path is a o c o d. The 2-component forest obtained from tau by deleting b is {a,c}, which misses the last component d; in every serial decomposition respecting the order a-c-d, the component that supplies the 2-component forest is last (or second after any merging), not first. Thus the assumed layout 2) cannot be enforced, and the recurrences that isolate the first subgraph do not apply to this spanning tree.

With terminals x,y, the y-coefficients are y_a=1 and y_p=y_q=y_s=-4/5. With terminals x,u, they are y_p=1, y_a=-5/4, and y_q=y_s=-1. These vectors are not scalar multiples, so the proposition is false.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: In all the experiments we have conducted for various $n$ and $k$, this value was equal to $\arccos(1 / \sqrt{n})$.

issues.failure_explanation: Distance(A) is the target function whose numerical value is an angle; the source states that the observed value is arccos(1/sqrt(n)). The algorithm, however, compares d with 1/sqrt(n) plus or minus epsilon. For n>=2, arccos(1/sqrt(n)) is strictly greater than 1/sqrt(n), so a true extremal subspace with d=arccos(1/sqrt(n)) and epsilon smaller than the gap enters the first branch, prints that the hypothesis is solved in the negative, and returns -1 instead of the promised set of extremal subspaces.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the threshold 1/sqrt(n) by arccos(1/sqrt(n)) in the two comparisons, or redefine Distance to return the corresponding cosine/norm quantity and use matching thresholds.
issues.overall_effect: The appendix algorithm's input-output contract is unreliable: it can misclassify the intended extremal subspaces as counterexamples to the hypothesis and fail to return the accumulated set.
issues.title: Algorithm compares angle to the wrong threshold
issues.why_classification: This is a local consistency error in heuristic pseudocode; a one-line correction restores the intended comparison without changing the mathematical architecture.
